improvements: The bot now accounts for naturally fast enemies, such as bats and crabs, when judging how quickly pursuers can close a short gap, even when no speed buff is visible.
incoming_learnings: Use the existing fast-movement species capability consistently when evaluating short pursuit gaps; an empty buff list does not make a vampire bat slow. Keep pursuit risk separate from current melee contact, and verify actual damage, defeat and pickup receipts. The isolated fixture demonstrates a different admitted selection, not encounter success.

review.review: The hero remained alive at full health when the planner stopped. A confirmed earlier use of the floor’s liquid-flame supply enabled an early departure shortcut. At decision 655, that shortcut preempted ordinary exploration despite 16 recorded frontiers and three unopened doors; mandatory strength discovery then blocked on missing flight preparation. All preparation alternatives declined, and no recovery descent occurred. The focused repair makes this early shortcut yield while ordinary frontiers or unopened doors remain, leaving action admission to existing controllers. A reduced public-coordinate regression fails on the original policy and passes on the candidate; the full suite passes (2282 tests, four skipped). This is not a recovered runtime-memory replay: the precise flight-demand path exclusions remain uncertain. The repair does not certify puzzle completion, identify the unknown potion, credit collection or establish eventual survival. Changed files are supplied through the trusted adapter.
review.learnings: A spent supply defers its own room, not all remaining floor exploration. Preserve ordinary observation opportunities before invoking departure-only strength discovery; keep mandatory pickup, protection and actual collection receipts unchanged.

recommendations.summary: Prevent one exhausted room supply from preempting unfinished ordinary floor observation.
